strings.Dos estudios de laboratorio pequeños, co: Two small laboratory studies, with two different measures: +9 and +10 bpm are the mean rises of two groups (Low 2008, 12 women) and +10 to +20 bpm are peaks (Kronenberg 1984, 11 women). The envelope joins the two: it is not a range measured in a single study. It is a peak of minutes, not a level: a hot flash in the small hours raises the rate enough to come out as an acute reading against the personal baseline.
strings.Un solo estudio de 1984 con temperatura: A single study from 1984 with oesophageal temperature (11 women): core temperature falls by 0.2 to 0.6 °C while the skin warms and sweats. A skin or wrist thermometer sees the opposite (it rises): see the skin temperature topic.
strings.Tres centésimas de grado de media (con u: Three hundredths of a degree on average (with a standard deviation of 0.12), and only in 51 % of hot flashes. The two sources agree on the direction and not on what it means: Freedman 2001 proposes that small rise as the trigger, and Jones 2019 concludes in its abstract «menopausal hot flushes are unlikely triggered by an increase in core temperature». It is far below what EMMA can tell apart from the noise of a thermometer.
strings.La piel del dedo sube de media 3,9 °C en: Finger skin rises by 3.9 °C on average in the hot flash (Kronenberg 1984). If EMMA one day read skin temperature from a wearable, each hot flash would be a peak of degrees, not of tenths.
strings.Un estudio grande con registro ambulator: A large study with 24 h ambulatory recording (215 women): vagal control falls during the hot flash, more so while asleep and in the younger women, also in hot flashes the woman does not notice. The abstract gives coefficients of a model, not milliseconds.
strings.Revisión sistemática con tres estudios e: Systematic review with three studies in the meta-analysis and a heterogeneity of 97 %: having hot flashes does not change the baseline variability that has been measured. What changes is the episode, not the level.
strings.Rango de 23 sofocos en laboratorio (medi: Range of 23 hot flashes in the laboratory (mean 3.4 minutes). Shorter than the window of many wearable readings: a hot flash fits whole inside a single sample.
strings.La medida objetiva de referencia del sof: The reference objective measure of the hot flash (sternal skin conductance) agrees with what the woman says in 29 % of cases outside the laboratory. EMMA does not measure conductance: what the crew member declares is the datum, and an undeclared HR peak cannot be attributed to a hot flash.
strings.Mediana de la cohorte SWAN; en quien emp: Median of the SWAN cohort; in those who started having them before or early in perimenopause, the same abstract says «median, >11.8 years». A three-year mission fits whole inside that window.
strings.Es una cota superior («up to»), referida: It is an upper bound («up to»), self-reported, from a review: it is not a prevalence measured in crew members.
strings.En la perimenopausia tardía la mayoría d: In late perimenopause most cycles are anovulatory (the same abstract: «Most cycles in late perimenopause were AO (>60%)»), and a cycle without ovulation does not have the luteal step in temperature: the variation by phase of cycle_physiology_read.json does not hold for it.
strings.En mujeres de mediana edad con ciclos qu: In midlife women with cycles that still oscillate, the amplitude of the temperature rhythm is as in young women (96 of the 116 had an oscillation; the abstract does not say how many from each group). The study excludes menstrual disorders and lasts one cycle: it does not measure irregular cycles.
strings.Cuello femoral (5,8 %) y columna lumbar: Femoral neck (5.8 %) and lumbar spine (7.38 %) in those three years. Of 10 years of loss (10.6 % and 9.1 %), most falls in the transmenopause.
strings.El informe de evidencia del HRP la da en: The HRP evidence report gives it on page 10; on page 8 it attributes it to a study of Mir cosmonauts (Leblanc 2000), which has not been read here. The same report says on page 42 that resistive exercise, with or without alendronate, attenuates it.
strings.«~10x», dice el informe de evidencia del: «~10x», says the HRP evidence report, with no citation of its own in that sentence; NASA's technical brief says that the trabecular loss of the hip in flight «might be analogous» to that of menopause. The two losses act through different pathways (loading and oestrogens), and nothing of what was read measures what happens when they coincide in the same person.
strings.Es lo único medido en vuelo con mujeres: It is the only thing measured in flight with women that has been read here: 9 astronauts on the ISS, the same response as the men. The abstract does not say the age or the menopausal status of any of them.
strings.Cuántos sofocos al día, medidos con un s: How many hot flashes per day, measured with a sensor and not by diary. None of the abstracts read gives a daily frequency: the review by Sievert 2013 says that reported frequency varies between populations and that comparing studies is difficult; that of Mann 2011 gives concordances, not frequencies; SWAN (Avis 2015) counts years with «frequent» symptoms (6 days or more out of every 14), not hot flashes per day. The PubMed search «hot flash frequency per day objective monitoring postmenopausal» (2026-11-15) returned treatment trials, not baseline frequencies.
strings.Cómo varían la temperatura basal, la fre: How basal temperature, heart rate or variability vary in irregular cycles of perimenopause. PubMed searches of 2026-11-15: «perimenopause wearable skin temperature irregular cycles» (0 results), «basal body temperature perimenopausal cycles» (3, none with a measurement), «perimenopause heart rate variability» (33: none follows the same woman through irregular cycles). O'Connor 2009 measures hormones in urine, not temperature; Alzueta 2024 excludes menstrual disorders and lasts one cycle; the review by Hira 2026 compares women with and without hot flashes, not cycles.
strings.Datos medidos en vuelo de astronautas en: Data measured in flight on astronauts in perimenopause or menopause, or on hot flashes in flight. PubMed, 2026-11-15: «menopause AND (astronaut OR spaceflight)» (17 results: bone reviews, that of Hart 2023 on loading, hormones and nerves, and the commentary by Rose 2022 on radiation; no flight data), «perimenopause AND spaceflight» (1: an aviation student with premature menopause), «female astronauts menopause» (4), «menopause AND astronauts AND bone» (4). NTRS (ntrs.nasa.gov), 2026-11-15: «menopause» (14 results; by title, bone, radiation and reproduction, and none announces data on menopausal astronauts; the three on magnetic resonance of the trabecular microarchitecture of the hip were not opened), «perimenopause» (0), «hot flashes» (12, none on human physiology). From the full text of Hughes-Fulford 2024, every sentence with «menopaus», «hot fl» or «vasomotor».
strings.En vuelo no se ha medido nada de la meno: Nothing about menopause has been measured in flight: neither hot flashes, nor the temperature or heart rate of a perimenopausal or postmenopausal astronaut, nor bone loss by menopausal status. What is written: that there are no formal in-flight data on the menstrual cycle because most use hormonal contraception (Hughes-Fulford 2024); that the bone response to flight was the same in 9 women as in 33 men on the ISS, without saying their menopausal status (Smith 2014); that NASA writes that lumbar loss in flight is about ten times faster than in early menopause (HRP evidence report) and that the loss of trabecular bone of the hip «might be analogous» to that of menopause (OCHMO-MTB-013); that the analysis of astronaut hip fractures could only be done with men, because with so few women their privacy was not preserved (HRP report); that the effect on bone of hormonal contraception in perimenopause is contested (Hughes-Fulford 2024); and, as one author's estimate without measuring anybody, that the radiation of a mission to Mars could halve the ovarian reserve and that this shortens the time to menopause (Rose 2022).
